reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to quickly identify potential spurious features through pattern recognition in the misclassified instances, while leveraging external XAI tools to objectively quantify feature importance and detect shared high-attribution patterns across all misclassified cases. This approach improves both efficiency and reliability in identifying columns with spurious correlations that are not semantically meaningful for classification.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify which features are present in all three misclassified instances (73, 291, 205) and evaluate their numerical ranges and trends across the instances
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features that appear in all three instances with consistent trends (e.g., increasing or stable values) and potential spurious associations

autonomous_tasks.query: Assess whether any of the shared features are semantically plausible (e.g., radius, texture, area) or likely to correlate spurious with malignancy/benignity based on medical domain knowledge
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of candidate features that are not semantically related to cancer classification but appear consistently across misclassified instances

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP, LIME, and Integrated Gradients provide model-agnostic feature attribution, allowing us to assess which features contribute most to misclassifications and whether the same features are highly important across all instances. Sensitivity analysis confirms whether removing a feature significantly alters predictions, helping to isolate spurious dependencies. Combining these tools across the misclassified instances ensures we detect shared spurious features with high confidence and drop out those with semantic relevance.
